newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia moves to curb TV sex and violence.
newsitem.headline: Colombia moves to curb TV sex and violence.

text.p: Colombia took action on Wednesday to curb sex and violence on television, introducing measures that could change the content of news programmes as well as some of the country's steamier soap operas.

The measures were announced by the state-run National Television Commission, which said censorship regulations were primarily aimed at protecting children during prime-time TV viewing hours up until 10 p.m.
In addition to a blanket ban on "pornography," the commission said any programmes featuring extreme violence would now be banned from family viewing hours.
It said a ban had also been placed on programmes depicting suicide "as a solution to human conflicts."

Colombia, a predominantly Roman Catholic country, is highly conservative in many aspects. But nudity and sex scenes are not uncommon in some of its more popular soap operas and violence -- including kidnapping and torture -- is a mainstay of many.

The worst violence is seen on the country's newscasts, however, and the commission said those too would have to adapt to the new censorship laws, which are expected to be officially promulgated within the next several days.

"In their coverage of cases involving extreme violence, suffering and death, news programmes should not enter into horrifying details or violate the victim's fundamental right to intimacy, dignity and privacy," it said.
Among other measures, it said broadcasts of close-up images of gory murder scenes were no longer permissible.

It also cautioned that whenever the government declares a state of "internal commotion" or limited form of emergency rule -- something not uncommon given its long-running war with leftist guerrillas -- TV newscasters were forbidden from broadcasting statements by rebels or anyone linked to "subversion or terrorism."
